name: Piezoelectric Synaptic Disruption Gauntlet
description:
The PSDG-2 is a contact weapon built around a lattice of synthetic piezoelectric crystal arrays embedded in a rigid gauntlet chassis. On impact, the kinetic energy of a strike is harvested and instantaneously converted into a precisely shaped electrical discharge delivered through conductive fingertip contacts. The discharge is not designed to cause cardiac disruption or burns — it is tuned to the frequency band associated with motor cortex signal propagation, creating a transient desynchronization of voluntary muscle control in the struck region. A blow to the shoulder renders the arm temporarily useless. A strike to the base of the skull produces full-body motor collapse for between four and twenty seconds depending on neural density.

The engineering challenge that Arcturus Defense Solutions spent eleven years solving was achieving consistent piezoelectric output across variable impact force. A glancing blow and a full-force punch needed to produce the same targeted discharge profile, or the weapon's selectivity would be meaningless. The solution was a tiered compression array that buffers excess energy into a capacitor bank and supplements insufficient strikes from reserve, meaning the PSDG-2 delivers identical neurological effect regardless of how hard the operator hits. This made it immediately attractive to operators who lack the physical augmentation typical of close-quarters specialists.

The nickname 'The Politeness' reflects the weapon's peculiar social niche: it is used extensively by corporate security personnel in environments where lethal force would be legally and reputationally catastrophic. A struck individual appears to simply stumble and fall, with no visible wound. The name 'Stutter' comes from the characteristic involuntary muscle tremor that affects targets in the recovery phase, which experienced observers recognize immediately.
specifications:
discharge frequency: Tuned to 40-80 Hz motor signal band
motor collapse duration: 4-20 seconds depending on target neurology
capacitor reserve: 12 fully buffered strikes before recharge
recharge time: 8 minutes passive / 90 seconds via dock
weight: 1.1 kg
coverage: Full hand and wrist to mid-forearm
compatibility: Requires neural handshake with operator's dermal interface for activation
tactical_use: Primarily used in escort, detention, and close-protection roles. Operators favor it for subduing targets without producing evidence of assault — the neurological disruption leaves no bruising or burns and resolves completely. In combat, it is paired with conventional restraint tools; the gauntlet drops the target, and the operator secures them before motor function returns. Experienced users learn to target specific nerve clusters to achieve selective disruption — a precise strike to the radial nerve cluster disarms without dropping, useful when a standing, cooperative subject is needed.
cultural_context: The PSDG-2 occupies an uncomfortable middle ground in GLMZ's legal landscape. Its license requirements are achievable by corporate security entities but deliberately out of reach for individuals, which means it has become a class marker — a signal that the person wearing it has institutional backing. On the street, it is sometimes called 'the corporate handshake.' Among civil liberties groups, it has become a symbol of plausibly deniable abuse, since victims often cannot prove they were struck. A small counter-culture has emerged around documenting the characteristic recovery tremor on video as evidence.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions executive protection details
story_hooks: A prominent labor organizer is found dead — officially from a fall, but the autopsy shows the neural disruption pattern consistent with a PSDG-2 strike to the brainstem, which should not have been lethal unless the discharge was deliberately overcharged.
A PSDG-2 surfaces on the black market with its neural handshake still active, locked to the biometric of a corporate security officer who was officially reported dead six months ago.
An operator is hired to retrieve a witness who was 'questioned' with a PSDG-2 and now has persistent motor disruption — either the weapon was defective or it was used far beyond spec.

Arcturus Defense Solutions quietly initiates a field recall, citing a 'firmware irregularity' — but the irregularity in question causes the capacitor to discharge into the operator's hand rather than the target.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting combat gauntlet that extends from knuckles to mid-forearm, resembling a high-tech MMA glove crossed with a neural interface device. The surface gleams with internal crystalline structure visible beneath semi-translucent panels. It has an aggressive, surgical appearance—all precision edges and purposeful geometry.
physical_description.dimensions: Glove span: 22 cm (knuckle to wrist), forearm coverage: 15 cm, overall depth at palm: 4.5 cm, finger-to-fingertip: 10 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and balanced despite the dense piezoelectric lattice—feels around 1.1 kg distributed across the entire hand and forearm, never accumulating dead weight at the strike point. Sits on the hand like precision sports equipment.
physical_description.primary_material: Rigid carbon-composite exoskeleton with embedded synthetic piezoelectric crystal arrays. Inner surface lined with conductive nano-mesh interface layer. Structural bracing uses aerospace-grade aluminum alloy.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray primary with brushed titanium accent striping along knuckle guards and wrist reinforcement. Semi-translucent resin panels reveal faint geometric crystal lattice patterns beneath. Minimal reflectivity—designed for low-light tactical work.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray dominant, titanium silver accents, with faint blue-white glow from piezoelectric charging indicators visible in the palm and finger contact zones
physical_description.grip_texture: Inner surface features advanced textured polymer with micro-grip pattern, wrapped at wrist with thin medical-grade silicone band for secure positioning. Fingertip contact zones are smooth, conductive polymer for neural handshake interface.
distinctive_features: Five small LED charge indicators running along the knuckle ridge—illuminate blue when buffered strikes are available
Semi-translucent crystal panels on dorsal surface revealing internal lattice geometry
Conductive contact nodes at each fingertip—subtle raised metallic points
Wrist-mounted neural interface pad with faint circuit etching
Heat dissipation vents along the forearm in geometric pattern
Impact-hardened knuckle guard with subtle Blackwood Commercial Group logo engraved
Micro-actuator texture on palm surface for optimal grip during discharge
Faint hairline cracks in the semi-translucent panels—intentional stress-relief design, not battle damage
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group logo subtly stamped on knuckle guard, barely visible in matte finish. Serial plate on inner wrist surface (typically hidden from view). Model designation PSDG-2 embossed along forearm brace in minimalist sans-serif font.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine, well-maintained. Corporate security weapons are regularly serviced and rarely show external wear. Charging indicators are routinely reset. The only sign of use is occasional micro-scratches on the impact zones and subtle discoloration where dermal interface contacts accumulate residue from repeated neural handshakes.
